newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine official says IMF talks preliminary.
newsitem.headline: Argentine official says IMF talks preliminary.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund team now in Buenos Aires is only preparing the way for a mission around the middle of the year to negotiate a new agreement, a top Argentine official said.

"This IMF mission will be here for 10 days and did not come to discuss the small print of the agreement, but just to establish a list of issues to be considered in the main accord," Economy Minister chief advisor Carlos Rodriguez told reporters late Monday.

"Our intention is to reach a three-year (Extended-Fund Facility) agreement, but if that is not possible we will have another one-year (stand-by) agreement. It is also possible that we have another (Extended-Fund Facility) without necessarily having to receive disbursements," Rodriguez said.
"We want to continue with structural reform and we want IMF auditing because we consider it best, as it forces you to define the situation over the next three years," he said.
A three-year agreement starting from 1998 to 2000 would provide an economic policy framework bridging presidential elections in 1999.
Issues discussed with the IMF team included changing the tax system to reduce payroll tax and other levies on employment.
"Taxes on work are a heavy burden on the poorest people, as what with this and value-added tax, the poorest end up paying proportionately more than the middle classes," Rodriguez said.
But he added the new agreement will probably not come before the present accord with the IMF expires in December.
"Having them back to back was a good idea, but we are not going to make it on time," he said.
IMF head Michel Camdessus, who is due to visit Buenos Aires for a bankers' meeting May 19, will not participate in any negotiations, Rodriguez said.
